summary: K0 remains minimal; distinction language is retained only as an interpretive layer. Toy output shows stable partitions under a persistence window, with no physical confirmation claim.
Attempted replacement of Theta0 fails because distinction needs an antecedent separation criterion. The safe result is primitive-boundary preservation.
Topos/contextual anchors support local assignment and global-obstruction vocabulary. Public use is appendix-only because the language would overburden K0 if inserted into core definitions.

Symmetry and gauge prior art provide typed comparison language for invariants, transformations, and order parameters. The deterministic toy run shows axis selection, but only as representation support.
QG anchors show a comparison space for locality, continuity, symmetry, state space, and background assumptions. The public claim is limited to comparison vocabulary.
